query: Why do some Amazon products receive predominantly negative reviews, and which factors contribute the most?

per_column.name: content_word_count
per_column.rationale: A mechanical length feature. Not a candidate cause of review sentiment nor a common cause of both a treatment and the outcome; at best a generic covariate/noise, not a genuine confounder.

per_column.name: has_complaint_language
per_column.rationale: Complaint language in the review text is an expression/reflection of the reviewer's negative experience, lying on the path between whatever real cause and the recorded label. It is essentially a proxy/mediator of the sentiment outcome, not an upstream common cause. Its extreme correlation with label_pos makes it near-outcome leakage rather than a confounder.

per_column.name: has_praise_language
per_column.rationale: Praise language is likewise an in-text manifestation of positive sentiment, essentially a proxy of the outcome itself, not a common cause of a treatment and the outcome.

per_column.name: has_negation_language
per_column.rationale: A surface linguistic feature of the review text; correlated with sentiment expression but not an exogenous common cause of any treatment and the outcome. Not a genuine confounder.

judge.rationale: The query asks which product-level factors cause predominantly negative reviews, so a valid causal setup needs a candidate TREATMENT (e.g., product attributes like price, category, quality, defect rate, shipping/delivery issues) plus CONFOUNDERS that cause both such a treatment and the sentiment outcome. None of the added columns supply this. They are all surface linguistic features derived from the review text (word count, complaint/praise/negation language). The complaint/praise features are near-proxies of the outcome (mediators/leakage), and word count/negation are generic textual covariates. No genuine treatment is present, and no variable qualifies as a common cause of both a treatment and label_pos. Therefore the causal-attribution claim is not realised.
